newsitem.title: USA: Fort Payne extends TVA contract 15 years.
newsitem.headline: Fort Payne extends TVA contract 15 years.

text.p: The Tennessee Valley Authority said Tuesday the Fort Payne Improvement Authority has signed a 15-year contract to buy power from TVA.
Fort Payne has used TVA power since 1938 and purchases about $16 million in electricity each year, TVA said.
TVA spokesmanm Craig Beasley said Fort Payne uses between 200 and 300 million kilowatt hours per year.
Its contract was to expire in 2000.

In return for the early renewal, Fort Payne gains access to TVA's industrial incentive rates including the Enhanced Growth Credit Program. Under that program, Fort Payne now can offer rate incentives to new or expanding industries, TVA said.

Located in DeKalb County, Ala., Fort Payne has worked with TVA to develop a diversified economy. As the world's largest producer of athletic and children's socks, Fort Payne has been nicknamed the "Sock Capital of the World."
It said "TVA's industrial price options will help us retain and expand our commercial and industrial base, and its technical assistance will ensure reliable service."
